articles.title: Why so many young people, not just the rich, are signing prenups and calling it 'intimacy'
articles.summary: Prenups aren't just for the wealthy anymore. For a generation shaped by financial upheaval and therapy culture, prenups are increasingly framed by zillennial...
articles.body:
Prior to saying "I do" in 2022, Roshni Patel and her partner had an important task they wanted to take care of: negotiating and signing a prenuptial agreement. For 28-year-old Patel, a prenup isn't just a contingency plan; it's something a bit closer to self-care.

"It's not about my partner," said Patel, who lives in Silver Lake and works in business operations. "It's about me knowing that I am doing my best to take care of myself, regardless of the situation." Patel is part of a generation approaching marriage — and the legal architecture around it — very differently than their parents did.

Society is in the midst of a zillennial prenup boom. According to a recent Harris Poll with Bloomberg , 53% of engaged or married Gen Zs and millennials have signed a prenup as of this spring. That's a striking increase from 2022 , when 39% of engaged or married 18-to-34-year-olds reported having one — and only 15% of engaged or married Americans overall did.

There are practical reasons for the boom. Zillennials, the microgeneration on the cusp of Gen Z and millennials, came of age during the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. Many watched their parents' marriages struggle and drew their own conclusions. In the last several decades, women's matriculation rates and early career outcomes have caught up to — and in some cases, outpaced — those of men, thus reshaping the calculus underlying many partnerships.

For some, the Great Wealth Transfer looms: an estimated $84 trillion moving from boomers to younger generations, reshaping what feels worth protecting before marriage. For others, the math is grimmer with student debt , an unforgiving housing market , fewer social safety nets and the enduring financial penalties of having children. Both roads lead to the same document.

But there is also something less tangible driving this shift. The prenup, long imagined as a wealthy man's hedge or a reluctant woman's obligation, has undergone a quiet generational reinvention , one that has just as much to do with attachment styles as it does assets.

Steeped in therapy culture and financial literacy content, young Americans are fluent in boundary-setting and open to frank conversations about money and mental load. They're now applying that framework to the oldest legal contract in the book. For them, financial candor before marriage isn't defensive or cynical — it's actually intimate .

Getting a prenup was a no-brainer for Patel. "Starting a relationship on this healthy, transparent footholding sets you up for success," she said. "We want to be with each other, but we also want to be smart about how we want to be with each other."

California's community property laws made it all the more salient for the couple. "In California, absent a prenup, your income from employment is community property: split 50/50 [in the event of a divorce]," said Jackie Combs , an L.A.-based matrimonial attorney and partner at Blank Rome LLP.

The same 50-50 split applies to debt, which was a key consideration for Patel, as her partner was starting law school and she didn't want to acquire his school debt if they were to divorce. In their prenuptial agreement, the pair agreed that any assets and debts prior to marriage as well as any assets and debts during the marriage are individual property, an intentional sidestep of California's community property default.

However, Patel and her husband added a "sunset clause" to their prenup, stating that after seven years or when they have children — whichever comes first — the provision of separate marital assets is effectively nullified. From that point on, all assets and debts would be shared.

Sunset clauses and so-called "trigger clauses" are growing more common , as they allow couples to add specific protections for life's many what-ifs, including, for example, if the couple decides for one spouse to leave the workforce. While lost earnings and career atrophy can be hard to truly quantify, more couples are trying to account for it in their prenuptial agreements.

For example, take Kirby Kimball and Carlos Real, a recently engaged couple in the process of moving from San Francisco to New York City.

Both agree that Real is likely to one day be a stay-at-home dad. "The work to raise a healthy and connected family and happy children is sometimes far harder than showing up to an office every day," said Kimball, 24, who works in public relations. "That should be appreciated and accounted for financially."

To Real, 24, who works in commercial property management, having a sense of security underscores intimacy. "The more that you have yourself secure, I think you can be more secure with each other and more open with each other," he said.

Getting a prenup used to be seen as "planning for divorce," said Combs, adding that the stigma is eroding.

According to Stephanie Coontz , one of the leading marriage historians in the U.S. and professor emeritus at Evergreen State College, "[Getting a prenup] makes perfect sense now for couples who trust each other very much — but trust each other enough to say, 'Well, things could go wrong.' "

To Coontz, candor is not at odds with care. "People have to get over the idea that there's something unloving about sitting down and saying what you want," she said.

Coontz's research over the last five decades traces the ways in which marriage has evolved throughout history. In her latest book "For Better and Worse" (2026), she references sociologist Andrew Cherlin's argument that marriage has evolved from "cornerstone" to "capstone." Once seen as the first step toward adult life, today marriage is what you do after you've already built one.

For Will Carragher, 24, a strategic advisor at an L.A.-based talent agency, this accumulation of life experience and savings is all the more reason to get a prenup. Carragher has been dating his boyfriend, San Francisco-based startup consultant William Smithers, 24, for two years.

"Men don't have any biological clock, so I have no timeline where I'm like, 'I want to get married by my mid-30s,' " Carragher said. "When you get married later in life, you have more time to build … retirement funds, Roth IRAs and investments. [Your] financial situation up to that point was very individual. I would probably want to have protection over what I've individually amassed."

As couples tie the knot later, there's often larger pots of "yours" and "mine" to consider before becoming one. And that's not to mention family wealth. To Luisa Valles, a 29-year-old architectural designer living in San Diego, a prenup can be a way to honor each other's families, by protecting what they built for their own children to inherit.

"Whatever we build together, we build together, and whatever we didn't build together is that. It's OK to protect both those things," Valles said this spring.

Since then, Valles and her partner with whom she was living have broken up. Splitting up with a long-term partner, she said, only underscores her belief that getting a prenup is essential. "If you think it's uncomfortable, if you think you can't talk to your person about that, then what can you talk to them about?" she said.

To Logan Crabb, 30, that same conviction coexists with old-fashioned romance. "I'm a very romantic person. I love love. I think marriage, in many ways, is a declaration of vows and commitment," said Crabb, an accountant from West Palm Beach, Fla., who, when we spoke in July, lived with her boyfriend of six years. The pair has since become engaged. "As much as I would love marriage to be exclusively that, it's not. … Marriage is legal, and it's medical and it's financial."

Talking about money (yes, really talking about it) turns out to be one of the more intimate things a couple can do. What negotiating a prenup demands, after all, is precisely what therapy demands: vulnerability, full disclosure and an explicit confrontation of what each person needs — or, even more intimately, wants .

"If you're going to go to premarital counseling with a priest or therapist, why wouldn't you also talk to a lawyer?" Combs said.

This framing of prenup-as-financial-premarital-therapy is mirrored in how young couples speak about the process itself, often directly borrowing from the lexicon of therapy.

"We tried to honor each other in how we wrote the prenup, in a way that felt mutually respectful," said Ruby Ross, a 28-year-old doctor living in New York with her 30-year-old husband, Brian, a facilities manager.

"It feels more like an act of kindness," Crabb said.

"With a prenup comes boundaries," said Valles. "Even just as a safeguard of self-protection and self-love, it's important to have those boundaries written down."

Not every couple takes that extra legal step before tying the knot. Katie Rocco, 30, and her husband do not have a prenuptial agreement. For them, open communication fills the gap. "It's a lot of frequent checkpoints as you enter each stage of your life that you couldn't anticipate beforehand," she said. "That's why you picked that person."

Rocco recently left her teaching job in Connecticut to stay at home with their toddler, and she acknowledges that these kinds of decisions rewrite the financial math in a marriage. When she and her husband recently refinanced their home — taking her name off the mortgage for a better rate — they agreed to maintain the deed in both their names. "I still want to have some ownership of this," she said.

For couples who take the legal step, a prenup is a way to put their intentions for the marriage into writing while things are still good.

"If there's a way to mitigate at least some of the financial discussions because it's already been set in stone when we were at the strongest point in our lives as a couple," Kimball said, "then we both want to take that step."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Incêndio em Bicas destrói casa durante a madrugada | G1
articles.standfirst: Causa será investigada, mas a suspeita do Corpo de Bombeiros é que o incêndio possa ter sido causado por um curto-circuito em um freezer. Ninguém estava no imóvel no momento.
articles.summary: Incêndio em Bicas destrói casa na zona rural. Causa será investigada, mas a suspeita é que o incêndio possa ter sido causado por um curto-circuito em um freezer.
articles.body:
Equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros combate incêndio em casa na zona rural de Bicas. — Foto: Divulgação/Corpo de Bombeiros

Uma casa pegou fogo na zona rural de Bicas durante a madrugada desta segunda-feira (19). No momento do incêndio, ninguém estava no imóvel . O caseiro da propriedade viu as chamas na sala da casa e acionou o Corpo de Bombeiros.

Segundo os bombeiros, casa era construída principalmente com madeira e foi totalmente tomada pelas chamas. — Foto: Divulgação/Corpo de Bombeiros

Ao chegar no local, a corporação confirmou que a casa, construída principalmente com madeira, já estava totalmente tomada pelo fogo . As chamas foram contidas e o rescaldo, realizado .

Causa do incêndio não foi identificada, mas a corporação suspeita que um curto-circuito em um freezer pode ter iniciado o fogo. — Foto: Divulgação/Corpo de Bombeiros

Os bombeiros realizaram uma busca no imóvel e confirmaram que não houve vítimas. A causa do incêndio não foi identificada, mas a suspeita é de um curto-circuito em um freezer que estava ligado à rede elétrica.

articles.standfirst: Anúncio foi feito pelo prefeito Leo Bezerra em vídeo nas redes sociais. Ponto facultativo seria na quarta-feira (28). Com a mudança, servidores municipais vão poder ter um "feriadão" até o dia 2 de novembro, da de Finados.
articles.summary: Anúncio foi feito pelo prefeito Leo Bezerra em vídeo nas redes sociais. Ponto facultativo seria na quarta-feira (28). Com a mudança, servidores municipais vão poder ter um "feriadão" até o dia 2 de novembro, da de Finados.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de João Pessoa anuncia transferência de ponto facultativo do dia do Servidor Público para a sexta-feira (30) — Foto: Secom-JP

A Prefeitura de João Pessoa anunciou a transferência do ponto facultativo do dia do Servidor Público para a próxima sexta-feira (30). O anúncio foi feito por um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais pelo prefeito Leo Bezerra (PSDB), nesta segunda-feira (19).

O ponto facultativo estava previsto para a próxima quarta-feira (28), no meio da semana. A mudança faz com que os servidores municipais tenham a folga na sexta-feira (30), próximo ao final de semana. O prefeito disse que a transferência teve como objetivo dar esse maior tempo de lazer para os servidores municipais.

"Duas notícias ótimas pra vocês. A primeira, que o feriado da próxima quarta-feira, dia 28, vai ser transferido pra sexta-feira, pra aproveitarmos o feriadão. E pra você também curtir a nossa cidade, que a gente tanto ama. E o salário vai entrar no próximo dia 30. Então é feriadão, com dinheiro no bolso", disse.

Com a alteração, os servidores da administração municipal vão ter um "feriadão estendido" até a próxima segunda-feira (2), data de Finados, outro feriado.

articles.title: Francisco Lino: morre ícone do samba e da cultura do Amapá | G1
articles.standfirst: Ícone da cultura amapaense morreu na noite deste domingo (18), aos 91 anos. O sambista compôs mais de 30 sambas-enredo para a escola de samba Boêmios do Laguinho, símbolo do tradicional bairro do Laguinho.
articles.summary: Fundador da Boêmios do Laguinho, Francisco Lino morreu aos 91 anos, deixando um legado de 35 sambas-enredo e décadas de dedicação à cultura amapaense.
articles.body:
Francisco Lino da Silva, morre aos 91 anos — Foto: Reprodução

Morreu na noite deste domingo (18), aos 91 anos, Francisco Lino da Silva, carinhosamente conhecido como Seu Lino. Ícone da cultura afro-amapaense e um dos maiores nomes do samba no Estado, ele foi um dos fundadores da escola de samba Boêmios do Laguinho e autor de 35 sambas-enredo da agremiação, tornando-se o maior compositor da história da escola.

Com versos que atravessaram gerações, Seu Lino ajudou a escrever uma das páginas mais bonitas do carnaval amapaense. Suas composições embalaram a trajetória vitoriosa da escola do bairro do Laguinho e contribuíram para a conquista de cerca de 20 títulos ao longo das décadas.

Entre suas obras mais marcantes está "Ritos e Mitos do Bairro do Laguinho" , samba-enredo campeão de 1963. A composição entrou para a história não apenas pelo sucesso na avenida, mas também pela forma como surgiu: foi escrita em apenas 50 minutos durante um voo entre Macapá e Belém .

A despedida dos desfiles veio em 1992, com o enredo "Que Fim Levaram as Nossas Pedras?" . Como em tantos outros momentos de sua trajetória, Seu Lino transformou poesia em samba e garantiu mais um título para a escola que carregava no coração.

Nas redes sociais, o Boêmios do Laguinho lamentou a morte do compositor. Em nota, a agremiação destacou que a "Nação Negra" está de luto diante de uma perda irreparável para a cultura amapaense.

Mais do que sambista, Seu Lino era um símbolo vivo da memória negra do Amapá . Guardião de histórias, tradições e saberes populares, atravessou gerações mantendo viva a identidade cultural do Laguinho, um dos bairros mais tradicionais de Macapá .

Sua trajetória se confunde com a própria história da comunidade. Entre rodas de samba, carnavais e encontros populares, viu o bairro crescer sem perder suas raízes, tornando-se uma das principais referências da preservação da cultura afro-amapaense.

Com sua arte e sua presença, Seu Lino ajudou a transformar o Laguinho em um dos mais importantes territórios de celebração do samba e da cultura popular no Estado. Seu legado permanece nos versos, nos tambores e na memória de quem aprendeu a contar a história do Amapá através do samba.

O velório ocorre em uma funerária no Centro de Macapá . A partir das 14h, familiares, amigos e admiradores poderão prestar as últimas homenagens na sede do Boêmios do Laguinho. O sepultamento está previsto para as 16h30, em um cemitério da região central da capital.

articles.title: Queimadas no Pará ameaçam rede elétrica e causam falta de energia | G1
articles.standfirst: Municípios do Baixo Amazonas e sudoeste do estado lideram focos de incêndio; fogo recente em Juruti deixou milhares de moradores sem energia.
articles.summary: Queimadas no Pará atingem a rede elétrica no Baixo Amazonas e sudoeste, provocando interrupções de energia em cidades como Santarém e Juruti.
articles.body:
Queimadas próximas à rede elétrica danificam postes e fiação no oeste do Pará; Santarém registrou 18 ocorrências neste ano. — Foto: Divulgação

Com o avanço da estiagem, o oeste do Pará e a região do Baixo Amazonas enfrentam um aumento preocupante de queimadas próximas à rede elétrica. Em Santarém , a concessionária de energia elétrica já registrou 18 ocorrências de fogo perto da fiação de janeiro a outubro deste ano.

Além dos impactos ambientais, o fogo danifica postes, cabos e transformadores, provocando interrupções no fornecimento de energia e colocando em risco a segurança dos moradores.

De acordo com dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe), o Pará registrou 8.625 focos de incêndio entre 16 de julho e 13 de outubro de 2026. Diversas cidades do oeste paraense e do Baixo Amazonas aparecem no topo da lista de queimadas no estado:

Fogo em Juruti interrompe fornecimento de energia

Recentemente, um incêndio florestal de grandes proporções em Juruti, no Baixo Amazonas, danificou a rede de distribuição e derrubou postes. O incidente, somado a ocorrências em Medicilândia e Colares, deixou cerca de 20 mil clientes sem energia elétrica por longos períodos.

"Quando as chamas atingem a rede de distribuição, comunidades inteiras podem ficar sem energia. Estamos falando de hospitais, sistemas de captação de água, escolas e residências que dependem desse serviço", explica Elton Lucena, executivo de Segurança da Equatorial Pará.

Em todo o estado, a distribuidora registrou 637 ocorrências de fogo que afetaram a rede elétrica de janeiro a outubro deste ano. Santarém aparece como a quarta cidade com mais registros (18 casos), atrás apenas de Belém (204), Ananindeua (140) e Benevides (30).

A concessionária orienta a população a adotar medidas preventivas para evitar novos incidentes na região:

Não queime lixo: evite usar fogo para limpar terrenos ou eliminar folhas secas perto de postes e fios;

Cuidado na área rural: mantenha materiais inflamáveis longe da rede elétrica e faça aceiros para proteger as propriedades;

Não jogue água na fiação: em caso de incêndio na rede, nunca jogue água nos cabos elétricos.

Ao identificar um incêndio que ameace a rede elétrica, a recomendação é manter distância e acionar imediatamente o Corpo de Bombeiros (193) e a Equatorial Pará (0800 091 0196).

articles.title: Pai morre afogado no Rio Poti e dois filhos seguem desaparecidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipes retomaram as buscas com três mergulhadores após os irmãos desaparecerem ao tentar socorrer o pai durante uma pescaria.
articles.summary: Equipes retomaram as buscas com três mergulhadores após os irmãos desaparecerem ao tentar socorrer o pai durante uma pescaria.
articles.body:
Pai é encontrado morto após afogamento no Rio Poti, em Teresina; dois filhos estão desaparecidos — Foto: Divulgação/CBMEPI

O corpo de Antônio das Dores Ferreira de Sena, de 43 anos, foi encontrado no Rio Poti, na região do bairro Ilhotas, em Teresina, na noite de domingo (18). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Piauí (CBMEPI), ele desapareceu após cair no rio durante uma pescaria. Os dois filhos dele continuam desaparecidos.

Pablo Vinícius Sousa de Sena, de 24 anos, e Vitor Dyerrisson Sousa de Sena, de 26, teriam tentado socorrer o pai após o acidente. As buscas pelos irmãos seguem nesta segunda-feira (19).

De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, Antônio das Dores caiu acidentalmente no rio ao lançar uma tarrafa de pesca, por volta das 17h de domingo.

Os filhos entraram na água na tentativa de resgatá-lo, mas também desapareceram.

O corpo de Antônio das Dores foi localizado por volta das 19h. As buscas foram encerradas às 20h e retomadas às 6h desta segunda-feira.

Segundo o CBMEPI, três mergulhadores participam das buscas por Pablo Vinícius e Vitor Dyerrisson.

articles.title:
Arujá terá primeira Fatec em 2027 e amplia oferta de cursos de qualificação profissional
 | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidade estadual vai oferecer 30 vagas para graduação em Análise e Desenvolvimento de Sistemas; município também prevê expansão do ensino técnico com nova estrutura do Senai.
articles.summary: Unidade estadual vai oferecer 30 vagas para graduação em Análise e Desenvolvimento de Sistemas; município também prevê expansão do ensino técnico com nova estrutura do Senai.
articles.body:
Prédio da Fatec será instalado no bairro Center Ville, em Arujá — Foto: Prefeitura de Arujá

Moradores de Arujá terão uma nova opção para cursar o ensino superior público a partir de 2027. A cidade vai receber sua primeira Faculdade de Tecnologia do Estado de São Paulo (Fatec), com 30 vagas para o curso de Análise e Desenvolvimento de Sistemas. Enquanto prepara a instalação da unidade, o município mantém programas de qualificação profissional e prevê ampliar a oferta de ensino técnico.

As aulas da Fatec estão previstas para começar no primeiro semestre de 2027. O curso será oferecido no período noturno, terá duração de três anos e incluirá disciplinas relacionadas a programação, banco de dados, inteligência artificial, computação em nuvem e segurança da informação.

As inscrições para o vestibular vão até as 15h de 6 de novembro. A prova será aplicada em 13 de dezembro, às 13h. A faculdade funcionará na Rua Othelo Melecsevics, no bairro Center Ville, com ensino gratuito.

A implantação da unidade envolve articulações entre a Prefeitura, por meio das Secretarias Municipais de Desenvolvimento Econômico e de Finanças, e o Governo do Estado. A expectativa é ampliar o acesso dos moradores à graduação tecnológica sem que precisem buscar essa modalidade de ensino em outros municípios.

Para o secretário municipal de Desenvolvimento Econômico, José Carlos, a chegada da instituição amplia as alternativas de formação na cidade. “A Fatec traz para Arujá uma nova possibilidade de formação, agora no ensino superior público. Ela se soma aos cursos e capacitações que a Prefeitura já oferece e cria mais oportunidades para quem busca qualificação profissional”, afirma.

Escola Técnica 4.0 formou 980 alunos em um ano

Antes mesmo da chegada da Fatec, Arujá já oferece cursos voltados à preparação para o mercado de trabalho. A Escola Técnica 4.0, que completa quatro anos, soma mais de 2 mil alunos formados. Desse total, 980 concluíram cursos no último ano.

A unidade concentra parte de sua formação nas áreas de tecnologia e em conhecimentos demandados pelo mercado de trabalho. Além dela, a Prefeitura mantém cursos gratuitos em diferentes segmentos, com iniciativas voltadas ao empreendedorismo e à geração de renda. Há também ações específicas para mulheres.

Outra mudança prevista é a ampliação da estrutura de formação industrial com a chegada de um novo Senai. A unidade deverá passar dos atuais 300 para cerca de 1.300 alunos atendidos por ano, com cursos direcionados ao setor industrial.

O prefeito Luis Camargo afirma que a implantação da faculdade ocorre em paralelo à continuidade das iniciativas municipais de capacitação. “A Fatec é uma conquista importante para Arujá. Ao mesmo tempo, mantemos nossos cursos e equipamentos de capacitação para oferecer diferentes caminhos de formação à população”, diz.

Com a previsão de início das aulas da Fatec em 2027 e a expansão da capacidade de atendimento do Senai, Arujá terá novas opções de formação em nível superior e técnico. A oferta se soma aos cursos gratuitos já disponíveis no município para quem busca qualificação, ingresso no mercado de trabalho ou novas possibilidades de renda.

articles.title: City halls torched, shops looted: France in shock after violent protest - videos
articles.summary: France witnessed widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police as nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions in
articles.body: France witnessed widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police as nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools escalated into violence, leaving businesses damaged and public buildings in flames. President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against rioters while announcing measures to address public grievances.The scale of the unrest was visible in Paris on Sunday, where shattered shopfronts, broken glass and dislodged cobblestones littered the area around Place de la République. Videos across social media sites also showed damage and looting in other shopping and tourist districts.Authorities estimated that around 5,50,000 people took part in Saturday’s demonstrations, while organisers put the turnout at 8,00,000. The protests were backed by labour unions, student organisations and activists seeking to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 over social injustice.Macron vows action as arrests mountIn a televised address, Macron acknowledged the public’s “anger” and “shame” over the unrest, while drawing a distinction between peaceful demonstrators and those involved in violence.“Those who looted will have to pay for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable,” Macron said.He also condemned what he described as “unrestrained violence” by “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”Social media has been flooded with viral videos of burning buildings, smashed storefronts and clashes, with users declaring “France has fallen” and warning that the country is on the brink.At least 2,400 people were arrested, according news agency AP. Macron said he had instructed prefects to work with mayors to protect public buildings and businesses, including by banning protests where necessary.City halls set ablaze, businesses lootedIn Limoges, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall on Saturday, causing its roof to collapse and nearly destroying the building. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate said “radical troublemakers” had broken in while officials, employees, security personnel and members of the public were inside.“They deliberately set the building on fire. It is an extremely serious and unspeakable act,” Barate said.In Marseille, protesters briefly entered the City Hall lobby, while a group damaged a police station. In Lyon, a fire broke out inside a tourist office.Paris mayor Emmanuel Grégoire described the damage as “considerable and unprecedented”, while stressing that the capital must remain a place where people can demonstrate and businesses can operate safely.Political blame and economic concernsThe unrest has also fuelled political tensions ahead of next spring’s presidential election. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen criticised Macron’s government, while left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon condemned looting and destruction.US president Donald Trump posted “France is burning!” on Truth Social, blaming immigration fro the protets and called on the country to “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” French authorities have not linked immigrants to the rioting.The unrest also weighed on the euro in Asian trading on Monday. The currency fell 0.1% to $1.1225, while the dollar index held at 101.83, Reuters reported.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US Immigration authorities return Indian national to Oregon jail over crash that killed newlywed couple
articles.summary: US authorities have transferred 32-year-old Indian national Rajinder Kumar to state custody in Oregon to face prosecution over a November 2025
articles.body: US authorities have transferred 32-year-old Indian national Rajinder Kumar to state custody in Oregon to face prosecution over a November 2025 tractor-trailer crash that killed two newlywed Americans, the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County, Oregon, on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person. The charges remain pending before the state court, and the allegations have not been established at trial.In a post on X on Sunday, October 18, ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Seattle office confirmed Kumar's transfer to the Deschutes County Jail, saying the move would allow state criminal proceedings to continue.“Two Americans lost their lives, and their families deserve accountability,” ICE ERO Seattle Acting Field Office Director Julio S Hernandez said, according to the agency's official statement.“ICE worked closely with law-enforcement partners to ensure Kumar is returned to state custody to answer for the serious charges against him,” Hernandez added, according to ANI.He further said, “This coordinated action protects the public, supports the victims’ families, and ensures that an individual accused of these crimes does not evade justice.”“ICE will continue using every lawful tool available to protect the American people from criminal activity committed by illegal aliens,” Hernandez said.According to ICE, the agency had lodged an immigration detainer with the Deschutes County Jail following Kumar's earlier arrest. However, the county released him in April 2026 without honouring the detainer, the agency said.“ICE officers subsequently located and arrested Kumar at large earlier this year,” the agency said in its post, without specifying the date or location of his subsequent arrest.ICE said deportation proceedings would remain on hold until the conclusion of the state criminal case. “Following the conclusion of state criminal proceedings, ICE will pursue Kumar’s immigration case consistent with federal law,” it said.The agency's statement also outlined Kumar's immigration history. According to ICE, US Border Patrol apprehended him near Lukeville, Arizona, on November 28, 2022, after he “illegally entered the United States from Mexico”.He was subsequently placed in removal proceedings. ICE said that “a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States”.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Japan’s MMX moon mission to launch on Oct 20, bring Phobos samples back by 2031
articles.summary: A Japanese space mission is set to lift off on October 20 with an ambitious goal: collect a sample from Phobos, one of Mars’ two moons, and bring it back
articles.body: A Japanese space mission is set to lift off on October 20 with an ambitious goal: collect a sample from Phobos, one of Mars’ two moons, and bring it back to Earth for detailed scientific analysis.If successful, the mission will mark the first time material from Mars or either of its moons has been brought back to Earth.Led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission is expected to reach the Martian neighbourhood in August 2027. Scientists hope the mission will help resolve a long-standing question about the origins of Phobos and Deimos.The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos while travelling through the Martian system before turning its attention to Phobos. The mission will deploy a small rover to survey the moon’s rocky terrain and help identify a suitable landing site for the main spacecraft.“No one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon,” Russell said, explaining that the competing gravitational influences make it difficult to place a rover safely on the surface.After the rover surveys the terrain, the spacecraft will descend onto Phobos and use a robotic arm and two sampling devices to collect material from the surface.The mission aims to gather approximately 10 grams of moon dust. The material will be sealed in a capsule and transported back to Earth, with the return scheduled for 2031. The capsule is expected to land in South Australia’s Woomera region.How did Mars get its moons?One of the mission’s primary objectives is to determine how Phobos and Deimos formed. Scientists are currently considering two leading explanations.According to the first theory, a large object struck Mars billions of years ago, scattering debris into space that eventually formed the two moons. The alternative explanation suggests that Phobos and Deimos were asteroids travelling through the Solar System before Mars captured them through its gravitational pull.Researchers expect the returned material’s chemical and mineral composition to help distinguish between the two possibilities.“When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results,” Russell said.Scientists have long sought to study samples collected directly from Mars and its surroundings, as laboratory analysis can reveal details that spacecraft instruments may not be able to establish conclusively.The MMX spacecraft is scheduled to launch from Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 am local time on October 20.You use AI every day. articles.title: Witnesses haunted by what they saw when pickup plowed through a Kansas youth soccer game
articles.summary: The crash at Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita killed a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man and injured several children and adults.
articles.body:
Witnesses of Saturday's deadly collision in which a pickup truck barreled through a youth soccer game in Kansas, killing two people and injuring nearly a dozen others, said they are haunted by what they saw and heard.

Cole Adrian, 6, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, were killed in the incident, which unfolded shortly before 3:30 p.m. at the city-owned Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita, police said.

The deceased were both from McPherson, Kansas, but were not related to each other, a Wichita police spokesperson said. Ten other people, ages 5 to 68, were also hit and hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries, Police Capt. Aaron Moses said.

Police said a dark Chevrolet pickup drove onto a field during a youth soccer game and struck children and adults.

Erica Case said it was halftime during her 9-year-old son's soccer game on an adjacent field when she first heard an engine revving, followed by several "boom" sounds.

"I saw the truck hitting things. I saw debris flying in the air," she recalled. "I don't know if it was a cone, a chair or a person, but you could see matter flying as the truck was barreling through the soccer field at a decent rate of speed."

"The moment that I recognized that that wasn't gunshots, that that was bodies, I lost it," Case said. "I lost it because it wasn't just adults. It was also children."

Case recalled the mother of another boy shouting that she was a nurse and needed to get to the injured. Case said she told her she would watch her boy and then took the woman's son to safety amid the chaos.

It took about 10 minutes for emergency services to arrive, she said, but people began helping the victims during that time.

"There are a lot of silent heroes that I know experienced much worse than I did, having to do mouth-to-mouth or CPR on somebody that'd been ran over by a truck," Case said.

David Griekspoor was at the complex with his nephew, who also plays soccer, when he witnessed the incident.

"It sounded like small gunfire," he said. "Bap, bap, bap."

He said it wasn't clear what was producing the sound until he focused on the truck. "You look up, and you just see the truck going through a line of people," Griekspoor said.

He said his brother and sister-in-law went to check on children nearby as he grabbed his nephew and "backed out of there." All ended up safe, Griekspoor said.

Police said they interviewed more than 30 witnesses.

The pickup's driver, a 34-year-old woman from Garden City, Kansas, was taken into custody but was later released after police consulted with the Sedgwick County District Attorney's Office. She has not been charged with a crime and has not been identified.

Police said the woman, who had two children in the pickup, had a child who had a soccer game on a different field at the complex.

The driver was cooperating with officers, said Moses, the police captain.

What caused the pickup to drive through the field was still under investigation, and police said the results of an examination of the vehicle, as well as of toxicology testing on the driver, were pending.

articles.title: Tiger Shroff shooting: Videos piece together moments before, during and after attack
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A series of videos has emerged showing the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area, including footage
articles.body: MUMBAI: A series of videos has emerged showing the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area, including footage capturing the moments when unidentified assailants opened fire at his car and the actor switched seats to take the wheel after his driver was injured.The incident took place around 7 pm on Sunday near Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, where Shroff was leaving after attending a birthday party. Seven shots were fired at the vehicle, injuring his driver, Firdaus, and a passerby identified as Umesh Charan.One of the videos circulating on social media captures the firing incident, with three men involved in the attack. Two of the assailants approached the vehicle on foot while a third waited on a motorcycle to facilitate their escape.The attackers opened fire as Shroff’s car was slowly moving out of the venue. The firing took place around 350 metres from Juhu police station.Another video shows Shroff switching seats with his driver after the shooting. A woman can be heard urging the actor to leave the spot, saying, “Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger”.Live Blog: Follow for updatesThe actor took control of the vehicle to rush his injured driver to hospital. Shroff and Firdaus were subsequently taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle for medical attention.The footage provides a glimpse of the immediate aftermath of the firing, as those present at the scene reacted to the incident.Shroff escaped without any bullet injuries, although he sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver suffered a gunshot wound to his left hand, while Charan sustained bullet injuries to his chest. Both were taken to hospital for treatment.In another purported video that went viral on social media, the gun appears to jam as the shooter attempts to fire the sixth shot. The other shooter then fires two more rounds, taking the total number of shots fired to seven.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has been linked to claims of responsibility for the shooting through a social media post and a voice note attributed to individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu. Police are verifying these claims and investigating the motive behind the attack.Also read - 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Khan in chilling audioMEanwhile, doctors said Charan was stable but required surgery. Firdaus was also being treated for his gunshot injury.Eyewitness recounts how the shooting unfoldedAn eyewitness who was present in the area described how the assailants positioned themselves before opening fire at Shroff’s vehicle.Rakesh Kumar, an autorickshaw driver, told ANI that three individuals were involved in the incident. According to his account, one person was on a motorcycle while two others were standing outside, with one near the gate and another positioned slightly ahead of it.Recalling the sequence of events, Kumar said, "I drive a rickshaw here in Mumbai... I arrived around 7:00 PM to take my vehicle out... There were three individuals involved: one was on a motorcycle, while two others were standing outside - one near the gate, and another positioned slightly ahead of it. When the shooting began, one person opened fire from the front, targeting the specific seat where Tiger Shroff was sitting... another person, the one near the gate, fired a shot that struck the driver in the hand. It happened around 7:00 PM..."Police form 15 teams to trace assailantsMumbai Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the shooting and identify those involved. Juhu police and the Mumbai Crime Branch are examining CCTV footage from the area to establish the suspects’ movements and escape route.The three assailants fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle. Police are also investigating whether Shroff had received any threats before the attack.The motive behind the shooting remains under investigation.Also Read: 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to SalmanLawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibilityTwo individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, purportedly took responsibility for the attack through a social media post and a voice note.The message alleged that Shroff had ignored warnings and also threatened people in the film industry who continued to work with actor Salman Khan.Police are verifying the authenticity of the claims and investigating whether the individuals who issued the threats were connected to the shooting. Their claims of responsibility have not been independently established.The incident has prompted concerns over the security of film personalities in Mumbai, following previous firing incidents targeting Salman Khan’s residence and other attacks linked to alleged gang rivalries.Fadnavis assures strict actionMaharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti to seek an update on the investigation and directed the police to take strict action against those responsible.Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”Police are continuing their investigation to identify the shooters, establish the motive and verify the alleged gang connection.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Companies exploiting welfare system by using residents as 'cash cows', BBC finds
articles.summary: Agents try to attract people on housing benefit by using social media videos that offer free rooms and holidays.
articles.body:
Some private companies are making huge profits and exploiting the welfare system by receiving housing benefits on behalf of residents but failing to give them the support they are required to, BBC Panorama has found.

Property agents are drawing people into the taxpayer-funded system using social media videos that offer free rooms, PlayStation consoles and even holidays.

The system - called supported exempt accommodation (SEA) - is designed for people in the UK with additional needs, including former prisoners, people recovering from addiction and women fleeing domestic abuse. It provides housing along with care, support and supervision.

For many residents it works well to help them get back on their feet, but charities, politicians and residents tell us parts of the system are being exploited.

There are often complicated, multi-layered financial and management arrangements in place.

Rather than going to residents, most welfare payments are made to non-profit registered providers. In many cases these providers then hire profit-making private companies to manage properties and deliver support.

Many vulnerable people are being used as "cash cows to generate income" that goes from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) into "the back pocket of the landlords", said Patricia Coleman-Taylor, who runs Birmingham anti-poverty charity Narthex.

Panorama has learned the DWP paid out £410m for SEA in Birmingham alone in the last financial year.

The city is the epicentre of the sector, with more than 34,000 people living in SEA. For context, in London about 22,000 live in supported housing despite its population being more than seven times larger.

Labour MP Jess Phillips, whose Birmingham constituency contains large numbers of these properties, said companies spending taxpayers' money while providing a poor standard of support was "an absolute catastrophe" and bad landlords "can make loads of money".

But she added that there are some housing providers who "get this money who are absolutely providing supported accommodation".

The leader of the city council, Liberal Democrat Councillor Roger Harmer, told us that "taxpayers' money is being wasted. It's a scandal."

In Birmingham, BBC Panorama's investigation found:

Vulnerable people are being left with little to no support in often unsuitable accommodation

One big housing provider wrote off £1.8m because of payments to some former directors and companies they ran

Evidence that some are willing to make benefit claims for people who do not live in their properties

Supported accommodation was set up for people like Alysha.

When she escaped a violent relationship, she returned to Birmingham seeking shelter. But her family did not have room so she had to look elsewhere.

Alysha lived in three different SEA properties, including a shared house managed by a company called Second City Support Ltd.

Things soon started to unravel, she told us. Last December, residents of the house went eight days without any heating or hot water when the boiler broke, she says.

"I was at my wits' end. I'd be begging [Second City] and they would just cut the call because they didn't want to deal with it."

As a survivor of domestic abuse, she also wanted help to get her life on track, including looking for a job, but said there was no support from Second City.

By law, the registered provider of the accommodation only needs to offer "more than minimal" care.

"On the [social media] adverts, they will often say that you have weekly support sessions, help with GPs. It's not the case at all, they're not interested. They come, they want you to sign a paper to say, yes, Alysha's gone to support [sessions] this week."

A closer examination of Alysha's shared house shows how taxpayers' money is used and how companies in the system can make money in other ways too.

The registered provider of the supported exempt accommodation was Dawson Housing, a not-for-profit.

Dawson Housing was being paid £443 a week in housing benefit from the DWP - which it received via Birmingham City Council - for Alysha's room and her support costs, equivalent to £23,000 a year.

Dawson Housing hired Second City Support Ltd to manage it and deliver her support.

Separately, a sister company, Second City Housing Properties, had bought and sold the house for a substantial profit.

Land Registry records show it bought the property for £191,000 in 2024 and sold it a year later for £410,000.

Both Second City companies are owned by Darren Davey. He told Panorama that his company had spent about £150,000 on renovation and other associated costs, prior to the sale.

Davey has been very successful in profiting from housing vulnerable people in recent years, operating in both the supported exempt and temporary accommodation sectors.

An analysis of his companies' records shows that over the past three financial years, Davey has paid himself £2.9m in dividends from his network of companies, as well as earning more than £900,000 in salary.

Davey said his salary and dividends must be considered in the context of his wider group of businesses. Any suggestion his earnings came entirely from supported accommodation "would be misleading", he added.

Lawyers for Dawson Housing denied Alysha's support was poor and say that regular in-person support was provided.

They said there were unavoidable interruptions in the provision of a dedicated support worker and that Dawson Housing accepted communications with her fell below the standard expected.

The lawyers added that Dawson Housing's records did not establish that there was an eight-day period without heating or hot water. They said there were several call-outs for a faulty boiler and remedial action was taken.

There are hundreds of managing agents like Second City in Birmingham.

Social media accounts, particularly on TikTok, are awash with companies trying to attract people on benefits into their properties, mainly clustered around Birmingham's poorest areas.

Panorama has also been repeatedly told about "ghost tenants" - individuals listed as residents but not actually living in properties, for whom managing agents still claim housing benefit.

A Facebook advert we saw had one man "looking for 7/8 ghost tenants in various houses of mine".

When we rang the number listed, a man told us he just needed Universal Credit details and National Insurance numbers.

The claims would be registered to rooms in his houses but "they wouldn't actually have to live there," he said.

He would effectively be receiving housing benefit for people who he was not accommodating or supporting.

Experts explain these individuals may offer respondents a one-off payment or a small recurring fee for using their details, while some people may never know their details are being used.

"That's fraud," said Jess Phillips. "Those people should go to prison."

Some people said they had been moved into SEA despite them not requiring support. Brian Edwards told Panorama he was one of them.

After a relationship breakdown, the 54-year-old former charity worker found himself homeless. Needing accommodation, he moved into a supported house provided by Windrush Alliance and managed by Nxtgen Housing Ltd.

He said he told Nxtgen that he didn't have any support needs but believes it applied for enhanced housing benefit on his behalf anyway.

Within a week, he had managed to get some contract work. He said that when he informed the agency, it told him if he worked, he would lose his enhanced housing benefit payment and become liable for his rent of more than £1,000 a month, or need to move.

A year and a half later, Brian said he was still unable to work and receives little support.

"If I work, I lose my housing. If I stay in my housing, I can't work. I've become trapped, not just trapped in housing, trapped on benefits."

Nxtgen Housing told Panorama it had "discussed different support plan options with Brian".

It said "he selected the support areas he considered relevant", and the support worker "subsequently worked with him on those plans".

Nxtgen said it did not discourage Brian from finding employment and improving his financial circumstances.

The government recently changed the rules to allow SEA residents to earn more without affecting their benefits.

Panorama has discovered that the provider of Brian's house, Windrush Alliance, had to write off £1.8m due to the actions of previous directors.

In 2024, a new board of directors at Windrush found "the company's current financial position has been compromised through an outflow of funds to former directors and companies under their control".

The "recoverability" of the payments was deemed by the directors to be "questionable," so the fees were written off.

Windrush Alliance did not respond to a request for comment by the BBC.

Five of the six largest SEA providers in Birmingham, including Windrush, have been deemed to be non-compliant with the standards set by the Regulator of Social Housing.

All five are still operating and receiving hundreds of millions of pounds in housing benefit payments. But the regulator announced last week that it was launching action to close one provider, Concept Housing Association, as it had "failed to address serious failings in the way it is run".

There is no single reason why Birmingham has become the centre of this issue. The availability of relatively cheap three-bedroom family homes - which can quickly be turned into five or six individual rooms with shared facilities - does attract landlords. But many also blame poor oversight from Birmingham City Council for allowing so many conversions to take place.

Another reason, said councillors and charities we spoke to, was that it is not actually council money that Birmingham is signing off but central government funding. The council simply approves the application - it does not have to pay for it.

Councillor Roger Harmer, a Liberal Democrat who became leader of Birmingham City Council after Labour lost power in May's elections, denied that, and told Panorama his officers were working to eradicate fraud and poor provision.

"There is a huge incentive for us to crack down on the bad providers," he said.

"But the problem is you shut down one property, they can just go next door and open up in the next house," he added, pointing out that housing benefit rules were set by the DWP.

In 2023, Parliament passed a bill to strengthen regulation of the supported housing sector in England. It included a new licensing scheme and a "fit and proper person" test. But more than three years on, the law is stuck in government consultations and has made no practical difference.

A government spokesperson said it is "working to implement measures... to raise standards and drive out the minority of poor providers taking advantage of the Housing Benefit system".

In Birmingham however, residents said they wanted action, not words.

Alysha said it is "shameful that people are being paid so much money. There's a lot of people who are vulnerable and in need. I'm going to class it as neglect."

articles.title: NHS bosses say smaller maternity units may have to close
articles.summary: The NHS Alliance said "difficult decisions" lie ahead and some maternity services may have to be consolidated.
articles.body:
NHS bosses in England say the way maternity care is organised is "not fit for purpose" with safety at risk, and warn up to 20 smaller units may have to close.

The NHS Alliance, which represents health managers, says difficult decisions lie ahead and maternity services need to be consolidated to support safer care.

It said a government taskforce into neonatal and maternity care must tackle key issues such as a lack of specialist staff and a rise in C-sections.

The Department of Health and Social Care said every woman deserves safe maternity care, and the taskforce "will deliver the reforms needed to ensure services meet the needs of women and families now and in the future".

The NHS Alliance said there are particular pressures on smaller units in rural and coastal areas and that those delivering 1,500 to 2,000 babies each year might need to close.

The organisation said up to 20 out of 155 consultant-led maternity units in England face closure. It says staffing problems and rising numbers of C-sections are making smaller units potentially unsafe.

The rise in C-sections was a challenge, according to the NHS Alliance, and there were inadequate operating theatres and beds in outdated and decaying buildings, posing a safety risk.

The NHS leaders' organisation also said some smaller units struggled to maintain safe staffing numbers for 24-hour care, including midwives and consultants such as obstetricians.

It goes on to say the government's taskforce must "grasp the nettle" by tackling these strategic issues, including significantly worse outcomes in deprived communities and raised maternity mortality rates for Black and Asian women.

The director of the NHS Alliance's acute and ambulance network, Matthew Hopkins, said: "Difficult decisions lie ahead, consolidating maternity services to support safer, more sustainable care."

He said any local plans had to involve NHS leaders, clinical staff, patients and communities, and that politicians "must have the courage to make the case for patient safety".

"It is time now to take a step back and consider how we should best organise maternity services across England, and where those services should be located", he said.

The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists called for "other solutions" to be explored that would prevent closing maternity units.

Dr Alison Wright, president of the college said the government should commit to "expanding the maternity workforce to ensure safe staffing levels, along with investment in training and retention of dedicated staff."

"The distinct needs and challenges of smaller units, especially in rural and coastal communities, must be recognised and supported," she added.

In August, a Devon trust suspended standard birthing services at a hospital in Barnstaple leaving pregnant mothers having to make a 53 mile journey to Exeter to give birth.

The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust said it was the "only safe course of action" due to staffing issues.

The trust added that it had explored every option including locum cover and support from other health organisations but that a temporary suspension was the best solution.

The North Devon maternity facility remains suspended with the trust saying there would be a "readiness assessment" later in October with patient safety the "overriding priority".

Campaigners say the delay is "disappointing". One couple told the BBC the thought of the longer journey for the birth of their second son had left them anxious and angry.

Catherine Mchomvu, chief executive of the Devon Antenatal Family Centre, has been campaigning to secure the future of the Barnstaple facility, and warned that reductions nationally would undermine the quality of care.

"If we had closures of smaller units you are going to find that women are not going to receive any level of continuity of care - that's purely because they are not going to see the same healthcare team more than once throughout the whole antenatal and post-natal experience", she said.

In June, Baroness Valerie Amos's review found women and babies were not being "listened to, heard or believed", with racism and discrimination "embedded throughout the system".

articles.title: China’s economy gains pace on exports as domestic demand falters
articles.summary: China's economy expanded by 4.5% in the July-September quarter compared with the same period a year earlier, supported by strong exports, official data
articles.body: China's economy expanded by 4.5% in the July-September quarter compared with the same period a year earlier, supported by strong exports, official data showed on Monday. The growth brings Beijing closer to achieving its annual economic target as the year draws to a close, even as trading partners intensify efforts to address their trade imbalances with the world's second-largest economy.The latest growth figure exceeded expectations and marked an improvement from the 4.3% expansion recorded in the April-June quarter, which was China's slowest pace of growth in more than three years, reported by news agency AP.Chinese leaders have set a full-year growth target of 4.5%-5% for 2026, lower than the 5% expansion achieved last year. Earlier this month, the International Monetary Fund lowered its forecast for China's economic growth in 2026 to 4.5%, placing its projection at the bottom of Beijing's target range.Strong exports support growth as domestic demand remains weakThe headline growth figure is becoming “an increasingly poor indicator of how the broader economy is performing”, said Max Zenglein, asia pacific senior economist at the conference board.According to Zenglein, the overall figure conceals widening differences across industries, regions and households. He added that Beijing faces difficult policy choices, with correcting domestic economic imbalances potentially proving more challenging than managing external pressures.China's domestic demand has weakened amid a prolonged property market downturn that has reduced household wealth and encouraged people to save more rather than spend.Exports, however, remain one of the economy's key sources of strength. China is on course to exceed last year's record global trade surplus of $1.2 trillion after exports rose 36% last month. Its trade surplus had already reached $938 billion between January and September.Higher US tariffs have disrupted some bilateral trade between Washington and Beijing, prompting Chinese exporters to seek alternative markets in Southeast Asia, latin America and Europe. High-tech products, including semiconductors, as well as automobiles, particularly hybrid and electric vehicles, have helped drive export growth this year.As China seeks greater self-reliance to reduce its vulnerability to western export controls and trade uncertainty, it has expanded manufacturing capacity across sectors such as solar energy and electric vehicles. These industries have also received substantial government subsidies.However, production capacity expanded rapidly while domestic consumption remained subdued, leaving manufacturers increasingly dependent on overseas markets to sell their goods at competitive prices.Ecaterina Bigos, senior market strategist at BNP paribas asset management, said China's export-led, technology-driven growth model had generated limited employment and broad-based income gains. She also warned that the risk of artificial intelligence displacing workers was increasing.European Union presses China to rebalance tradeChina's growing exports of relatively inexpensive manufactured goods have raised concerns among trading partners about the pressure on their domestic industries and economies.Eswar Prasad, a professor of economics and trade policy at Cornell University, said it was unsustainable for the world's second-largest economy to depend on foreign demand to support its growth.He argued that China's persistent and substantial trade surpluses had become a drag on global growth rather than helping drive expansion in other economies.The European Union is among the trading partners seeking to narrow the imbalance. The 27-member bloc runs a trade deficit with China exceeding $1.1 billion a day, while Chinese exports to the EU increased 16% during the first nine months of the year.European countries are considering further restrictions on Chinese products after the EU and China reached an agreement this month aimed at roughly halving the number of Chinese hybrid vehicle imports over the next few years.Gary Ng, a senior Asia Pacific economist at French bank Natixis, said China wanted to maintain access to overseas markets and could work with other countries to resolve trade disputes. An agreement on hybrid vehicles, for instance, could allow Chinese manufacturers to continue expanding sales in Europe over the longer term while avoiding a broader increase in tariffs.Nevertheless, Lynn Song, chief economist for greater China at Dutch bank ING, cautioned that trade imbalances would be difficult to correct quickly, even if agreements were reached.Some policymakers have also argued that the yuan's undervaluation against the US dollar and the euro has contributed to China's growing trade surplus. China's central bank has rejected these claims.Bigos said economies around the world were likely to maintain resistance to Chinese exports, with protectionist measures and pressure to safeguard domestic industries and employment expected to persist, particularly in high-value sectors.Beijing has maintained that it does not seek to generate a large trade surplus. On Friday, People's bank of China governor Pan Gongsheng said countries running trade deficits and those recording surpluses should work together. He added that China, as a responsible country, remained committed to expanding domestic demand.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: The kingmakers who could determine Israel’s election
articles.summary: Israel’s Arab-led and ultra-Orthodox parties face attacks but could hold the balance of power after October 27 vote.
articles.body:
In the run-up to Israel’s high-stakes election , few parties have featured more often in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s attacks on rivals than Ra’am and the Joint List.

Together, the two parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population, are projected to win 13 seats. If this is confirmed at the October 27 polls, the Arab-led lists could be critical to any post-election coalition, regardless of its political stripe.

In 2021, Ra’am made history by becoming the first Arab party to enter an Israeli government after joining a broad coalition that briefly removed Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu had previously shown himself ready to negotiate terms for a potential government with Mansour Abbas , the leader of Ra’am, or the United Arab List. But instead, Abbas joined forces with the coalition of Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid to try to drive through some of the measures he had campaigned for.

This time, both the Netanyahu camp and most leaders of the self-styled Zionist opposition bloc have ruled out forming a government with the parties representing Palestinian citizens. Still, Netanyahu and his allies have sought to portray their political opponents as beholden to the Arab-led lists, while the opposition has been attacking them for their reliance on the minority ultra-Orthodox parties to maintain their own power base.

Opinion polls have consistently indicated that Netanyahu’s Likud party and the far-right coalition it leads are running neck-and-neck with the Zionist opposition bloc, with neither side on track to win an outright majority in the 120-strong Knesset.

“Netanyahu would work with Ra’am in a heartbeat, if it meant staying in power,” said Yossi Mekelberg, a Middle East analyst at Chatham House.

“The opposition, too, don’t seem to understand the consequences of their actions,” he said of repeated attempts across the opposition bloc to undermine the credibility of what may be a future plank in any government.

“If it came down to it, of course they’d accept the support of the party they’d previously vilified without thinking of how that will undermine their government, and undermine the votes of the large numbers of Arab Israelis who support them,” added Mekelberg.

In the lead-up to the polls, Likud has repeatedly used hard-hitting attack adverts to warn that if Netanyahu is voted out, it will be the Arab parties that would emerge as kingmakers in a new government potentially led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party.

“There is no Gadi without [Ahmad] Tibi,” said a Likud campaign slogan in reference to the leader of Ta’al, one of three parties comprising the Joint List.

The alliance, which also includes the Hadash and Balad factions, has said it could provide a so-called safety net to the anti-Netanyahu coalition by agreeing not to stand against it in a confidence vote, even if the alliance does not join the government. In return, it has said it would demand certain conditions, including a path to Palestinian statehood and fighting organised crime.

Combatting the wave of violent crime that has been allowed to engulf Palestinian communities, as well as addressing discriminatory government policies, including on housing, have also been the focus of Ra’am ahead of the election.

Established in 1996, the party has already distanced itself from its religiously conservative foundations. In December 2025, Abbas said the party’s political decision-making body would separate from its religious council. Eight months later, it selected its electoral list independently for the first time and placed the Jewish Zionist Yoav Segalovitz , a former senior police commander and deputy public security minister in the Bennett-Lapid government, second on its slate.

Describing Ra’am as “one of the most interesting parties” of this year’s election, Mekelberg said: “Through Mansour Abbas, they are continually reinventing themselves without appearing opportunist.”

The upcoming election is the first since the Hamas-led attack in southern Israel of October 7, 2023 that led to the killing of an estimated 1,200 people, and triggered Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

The war has also sped up a political shift to the right, with Arab-led parties increasingly targeted by right-wing figures seeking to cast them as complicit in the October 7 assault.

In May, Bennett apologised for going into government with Ra’am, while in September, Netanyahu’s Likud and the Otzma Yehudi party of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir petitioned to bar Ra’am and the Joint List from the election.

On September 23, the Central Elections Committee, whose members are drawn from the Knesset’s parties, voted to disqualify both lists, as well as two individual candidates.

Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh was to be barred over an article he wrote on October 8, 2023 describing the Hamas-led attack of the previous day as an “important historic event”. Ofer Cassif, a Jewish politician with Hadash, was targeted in a petition filed by Likud that cited legal prohibitions on candidates who support “an armed struggle by an enemy state or terrorist organisation against the State of Israel”.

On October 2, the Supreme Court unanimously overturned the disqualifications of the Joint List and Ra’am, as well as Cassif’s, by a 7-2 majority. Abu Shehadeh had withdrawn his candidacy a day earlier, after it became clear the court was likely to uphold his disqualification.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, Cassif later called it “a political decision far more than a judicial one”, driven by “fear that they’re going to need us”.

Orly Noy, a Balad candidate and the first Jewish politician to be voted onto the party list’s top five, said it was “safe to say” that the alliance is not going to be part of the next ruling coalition.

“It depends if the other parties want to prioritise the wishes of their voters or their own racism. However, even if we’re excluded, we can still gain concessions from any coalition in return for our support,” she added. “That might not mean ending the occupation, which of course would be ideal, but there’s a lot we can still do that will make people’s lives better.”

The taint of October 7 has not only extended to Arab parties unconnected to the events of that day, but also to ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.

As routine partners in Likud’s governing coalitions, they have faced accusations by many leading opponents of draft-dodging, while drawing heavily on what many regard as a generous state welfare package.

Israel’s ultra-Orthodox community is largely represented by two parties: Shas, which draws on Jews of Spanish, North African and Middle Eastern descent; and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), comprising Jews of central and eastern European descent. Each is polling at about seven or eight seats.

Rather than focusing on foreign policy and taxation, their core aims tend to be shielding ultra-Orthodox students from military service, securing welfare support for the large families common in the community, where many men study rather than work, and protecting state funding for their schools and institutions.

Long seen as Netanyahu’s most dependable allies, they broke with Likud last year over its failure to legislate an exemption to the draft. The UTJ left the coalition altogether, while Shas quit the government but did not pull its 11 politicians out of the parliamentary coalition. Shas later gave up its coalition committee roles, and both parties boycotted coalition bills.

Nevertheless, the support of the ultra-Orthodox has come with a political price tag. In January, opposition leader Yair Lapid accused the government of sending billions “to the corrupt and [the] draft dodgers” while another possible contender for the premiership, the right-wing Avigdor Lieberman, who heads the Yisrael Beytenu list, likened Shas and UTJ to the Taliban over their lack of female representation.

articles.title: Bombay HC to hear on October 26 plea filed by actor Imran Khan against 'Leave India' order
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Monday said it will hear on October 26, actor Imran Khan Pal’s petition against a ‘leave India notice’ issued by the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Monday said it will hear on October 26, actor Imran Khan Pal’s petition against a ‘leave India notice’ issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer, (FRRO), Mumbai, to him on October 14, four days after a protest where he was detained. The notice requires him to leave the country, as a US national, by October 28.The HC asked the actor to also make State a party.Senior counsel Venkatesh Dhond for the actor mentioned the matter for urgent hearing. He said, “ this is a petition where a person who has been residing in India since he was 2 years old, is asked to leave without notice, without any hearing, without reasons…”.The actor has no criminal antecedents, Dhond said to a query. He said the petition mentions that he has no criminal record and no antecedents.The Chief Justice led bench before which the matter was mentioned asked if all parties were served a copy of the petition. Dhond said it was. The Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh for the Centre and FRRO, a central authority under the Bureau of Immigration said he received a copy of the petition “10 minutes ago.”Dhond sought a hearing the day after. Singh said it can be heard on October 26.Dhond said since the actor has been asked to leave by October 28 it would be cutting it too close. However, Singh said, “we will come prepared to argue the matter.”The actor, almost 44, had filed the petition on Saturday challenging the notice as “arbitrary, unreasoned and wholly misconceived’’ and against principles of natural justice.The notice flouts his fundamental rights to equality under Article 14 and to life under article 21 of the Indian constitution, his lawyers contended.On Saturday the actor also was issued a fresh notice this time a show cause notice on why his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status should not be cancelled by invoking a provision under the Citizenship Act that says for any action violatingArticles 14 and 21 are constitutional guarantees available to even foreigners in India, it underscored. He was given no reasons nor any reasonable opportunity to be heard and the notice was issued directly, the petition argued.The FRRO, had within four days of a protest in Mumbai against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, where the actor was present, invoked the Immigration and Foreigners Act (IFA) 2025 to issue him the departure notice on October 14. The notice is based on “purported contravention of uncited provisions of the IFA and the Rules and Orders’’ under it.His petition says , Merely …mechanically reproducing the words of a statutory provision is not sufficient in law and cannot be countenanced” It take a ground that the actor “who has lived in India for forty-two years, is apparently sought to be expelled solely because an FIR has been registered. The FIR is at the stage of investigation.The offences alleged under Sections 223, 126(2), 189(2), 189(3) and 189(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are all bailable, and none carries a punishment exceeding two years. No charge-sheet has been filed, no court has taken cognizance, and no charge has been framed.Even if a charge-sheet were to befiled, the Court may decline to take cognizance. If it takes cognizance, the Petitioner may be discharged. If charges are framed, he may be acquitted.To expel the Petitioner at the very threshold of that process is to visit the ultimate consequence upon a mere allegation and to condemn him, in effect, on the mere recording by the police of an intimation of the commission of an offence.”The urgent interim relief the actor will argue for next Monday is a stay of the notice and final relief is to quash and set it aside.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news.
